claim: LISA is a plug-and-play attention replacement that requires no pretraining from scratch: a linear attention branch (O(n)) runs in parallel with a lightning indexer that selects top-M tokens for sparse self-attention, fused by a gate, reducing inference from O(n^2) to O(nM).
stance_target: The claim that sparse attention can be retrofitted onto an existing model rather than requiring from-scratch sparse pretraining
quoted_support: we propose LISA (Linear-Indexed Sparse Attention), a plug-and-play attention replacement module that requires no pretraining from scratch. ... reducing inference complexity from O(n2) to O(nM) (M << n) for generating n tokens.

claim: LISA freezes all original model parameters and trains only the newly added linear-attention and indexer modules, which is what gives it the plug-and-play property and avoids catastrophic forgetting.
stance_target: The frozen-parameters retrofit strategy as an alternative to full-model sparse pretraining
scope_conditions: Two-stage training; Stage 1 freezes all original parameters
quoted_support: During training, we freeze all original model parameters and only train the newly added linear attention parameters. ... The training strategy of LISA freezes all original parameters of the main model, only training the newly added linear attention and Indexer components.

claim: Because top-M selection is argmax, gradients cannot flow back to the indexer; LISA therefore trains it with a per-head KL divergence loss against the teacher's attention patterns, plus candidate dropout (top-1.2M candidates with 20% random masking early, decaying) and z-loss to prevent collapse onto early tokens.
stance_target: The repo's claim that top-k selection is non-differentiable and requires a separate distillation loss
scope_conditions: Stage 2 training; per-head KL divergence loss
quoted_support: due to the top-M (argmax) strategy, training gradients cannot flow back to the Indexer module. claim: Attention-mass capture (MASS) reaches 80% at M=256, only 6% below the oracle upper bound; it falls to 70% at M=128 and rises to 88% at M=512, making M=256 the recommended budget.
stance_target: What top-M budget is needed for sparse attention to preserve the full-attention distribution
scope_conditions: MASS metric defined as captured attention mass over the oracle top-M weights
quoted_support: at M = 256, the MASS reaches 80%, trailing the theoretical upper bound (defined by the oracle's top-M weights) by only 6%. Performance scales predictably with the budget: the metric decreases to 70% at M = 128 and improves to 88% at M = 512.

claim: LISA achieves a 50% inference speedup at 16K-token context while improving average reasoning accuracy by 5.6% on DeepSeek-distilled Qwen models.
stance_target: Whether sparse attention can improve quality and speed simultaneously at moderate context
scope_conditions: DeepSeek-distilled-Qwen models; AIME, MATH-500 and related reasoning benchmarks
quoted_support: Experiments on DeepSeek-distilled-Qwen models demonstrate that LISA achieves a 50% inference speedup under 16K-token context, while improving average performance by 5.6% on reasoning benchmarks including AIME and MATH-500.

claim: Each of LISA's two training stages takes approximately 240 GPU-hours on an NVIDIA H100 for the 7B retrofit, i.e. roughly 480 H100-hours total — a concrete anchor for the cost of retrofitting sparse attention onto a 7B model.
stance_target: The training cost of a sparse-attention retrofit at 7B scale
scope_conditions: Qwen2.5-7B; Stage 1 LR 2e-5, batch 128, 2 epochs, 50-step warmup; Stage 2 1 epoch
quoted_support: This stage takes approximately 240 GPU hours on an NVIDIA H100. ... taking approximately 240 GPU hours on an NVIDIA H100.

claim: LISA's Stage 1 replaces the teacher's standard attention with a fixed-budget sliding window of size M plus a linear attention branch, and retains the original standard attention every 6 layers to preserve exact retrieval capability.
stance_target: How much full attention must be retained when retrofitting sparse attention
scope_conditions: Stage 1 architecture; every 6th layer keeps standard attention
quoted_support: we replace the standard attention in the teacher model with our linear attention variant while retaining the original standard attention every 6 layers to preserve exact retrieval capability.
